name: Quadratic assignment: QAPLIB tai256c
description: Assign the 256 facilities of the QAPLIB instance tai256c to 256 locations so that the sum of flow times distance is as small as possible. The best known assignment costs 44,759,294 and no optimality proof exists.

sources.locator: QAPLIB deposit (CC BY 4.0): tai256c.dat in qapdata.tar.gz (SHA-256 e7d72083d49f4768...) and the best known permutation tai256c.sln in qapsoln.tar.gz; the README table lists 44759294 for tai256c.
Burkard, Karisch and Rendl (1997), QAPLIB - a quadratic assignment problem library: instance definitions and conventions.
Koopmans and Beckmann (1957), Assignment problems and the location of economic activities: the quadratic assignment model.

K. Fujii, S. Kim, M. Kojima, H. D. Mittelmann, Y. Shinano (2024), An exceptionally difficult binary quadratic optimization problem with symmetry: a challenge for the largest unsolved QAP instance Tai256c.

requirements.datasets: QAPLIB instance tai256c.dat from the Edinburgh DataShare deposit (CC BY 4.0), fetched and SHA-256 checked by scripts/prepare_frontier_combinatorics.py into data/frontier_combinatorics/ of the task cache (ARENA_TASK_CACHE_DIR, default ~/.cache/empira/tasks).

evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: solve(a, b) -> permutation p of 0..n-1 (list of n integers); a and b are this task's QAPLIB matrices (int64 NumPy arrays of shape (n, n), first and second matrix of the instance file, passed as copies). Facility i is placed at location p[i]. Score: the exact integer cost sum_{i,j} a[i, j] * b[p[i], p[j]], minimized. The instance file is read from the prepared data directory and its SHA-256 is checked before every evaluation.

limitations: Branch-and-bound lower bounds are within about 1.25% (Fujii, Kim, Kojima, Mittelmann and Shinano, 2024); QAPLIB's bound is 43,849,646.
The instance file is fetched by scripts/prepare_frontier_combinatorics.py and pinned by SHA-256; the evaluator refuses a file with another digest.

The record construction is public, so a candidate can reproduce the record by embedding it; the score measures the returned object, not the search that produced it, and only a strictly smaller score than the best known value is a new result.
Candidate Python runs inside the evaluator process as trusted research code; the evaluator recomputes every property of the returned object exactly and trusts nothing the candidate reports.

state_of_the_art.statement: The best known solution of Taillard's grey-density instance tai256c (the largest unsolved QAPLIB instance) costs 44,759,294; it was found by an ant-colony algorithm (QAPLIB code ANT, T. Stuetzle's MAX-MIN ant system, 1997) and is recorded in QAPLIB. Branch-and-bound lower bounds are within about 1.25% (Fujii, Kim, Kojima, Mittelmann and Shinano, 2024); QAPLIB's bound is 43,849,646. No later improvement was found in the literature reviewed on 2026-10-12.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a minimum-cost Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment of facilities to locations for the QAPLIB instance tai256c.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The quadratic assignment problem models facility and hospital layout, keyboard design, backboard wiring and turbine balancing. It is NP-hard and notoriously difficult in practice: QAPLIB instances above about 40 facilities remain unsolved, and the best known solutions of the large instances have resisted improvement for decades, so a cheaper permutation is a new best known solution of a standard open instance.

papers.title: Assignment problems and the location of economic activities
papers.primary_goal: Formulate the assignment of indivisible economic activities to locations, introducing the quadratic assignment problem.
papers.task_relation: The task's objective is the Koopmans-Beckmann quadratic assignment cost on the QAPLIB instance tai256c.

papers.title: An exceptionally difficult binary quadratic optimization problem with symmetry: a challenge for the largest unsolved QAP instance Tai256c
papers.primary_goal: Solve or tightly bound tai256c, the largest unsolved QAPLIB instance, by reformulating it as a binary quadratic problem and exploiting its symmetry in branch and bound.
papers.task_relation: The paper's object is exactly this instance; its lower bound leaves a gap of about 1.25% to the best known cost 44,759,294 that the task asks to reduce from above.

science_relevance.reason: Both papers have the quadratic assignment problem (and, for the second, this instance or the search for its best solutions) as their main objective; the evaluator scores exactly the QAP cost of a permutation on the pinned instance.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata inspected; the best known value read from the QAPLIB deposit (README table and solution file) and from the DLAS study's table (arXiv:1806.09328); the published permutation re-scored with the evaluator.
